cases.description: Five executions pass against the recording.
Five failures against the recording: p = 1/252.
Four failures in five: p = 6/252.
Two failures in five are not significant: p = 56/252, flaky, paraphrase needed.
One failure is never a regression.
Two executions that both fail are not enough: p = 1/6.
Infrastructure errors never fail an assertion and are counted apart.
No completed execution is an infrastructure error.
Three failures and two infrastructure errors: the errors do not count as failures.
One pin mismatch makes the scenario pin_mismatch, whatever the rest.
A pin mismatch outranks a regression in the same scenario.
not_checked outcomes are neither passes nor failures.
Two not_checked and three failures: three failures in three checks.
A run that fails as often as its baseline did is flaky, not a regression.
Against a baseline of 3 in 5, five failures give p = 21/252.
Against 10 passes in 10, three failures in five: p = 66/3003.
A significant but small drop (below 0.2) is flaky.
The same run size with a drop of 0.3 is a regression.
An assertion the baseline run lacks is compared with the recording.
A run better than its baseline passes.
One regressed assertion among passing ones makes the scenario a regression.
A flaky assertion beside passing ones makes the scenario flaky.
Paraphrased executions count with the others.
Two failures in twenty against 20 of 20: p = 380/1560, flaky.
